canonical_statement: Let $f(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that\[n! = a_1\cdots a_k\]with $n< a_1<\cdots <a_k=m$. Is there (and what is it) a constant $c$ such that\[f(n)-2n \sim c\frac{n}{\log n}?\]

definitions:
Formal-semantics guard: for this frozen source record the current Lean target signature is exactly `theorem erdos_390 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c,
      (fun n => f n - 2 * n : ℕ → ℝ) ~[atTop] (fun n => c * n / log (n : ℝ))`. Its binder types, predicate meanings, coercions, filters, and endpoint conventions control any machine-level reformulation; the prose statement may not be used to weaken them.

Quantifier-order guard: the quantifiers occur in the order stated and may not be commuted, weakened, or replaced by sampled cases. Salient source phrases include: Is there (and what is it) a constant $c$ such that\.

Asymptotic-notation guard: `~`, `o`, `O`, `≪`, and `≫` keep their standard distinct meanings. Any hidden constant may depend only on parameters explicitly shown as subscripts/fixed before the limiting variable, never on the limiting variable itself.

Sequence guard: preserve monotonicity, strictness, indexing origin, recurrence/greedy rule, and whether the sequence is uniquely determined or existentially chosen. Finite-prefix agreement is not eventual/global agreement.

Extremal guard: minimum/minimal and maximum/maximal are different notions. When a numerical extremum is requested, a close needs both an attaining construction/witness (or exact existence) and a proof that no better value is possible.
invariants_that_must_survive_every_refor: The canonical statement text is immutable; every proof target must imply exactly that statement (or its literal negation for a negative close).
Every quantifier, domain, hypothesis, strict/non-strict inequality, endpoint, normalization, and parameter dependency survives every reformulation.
Discrete structure is preserved: integrality, distinctness, ordering, multiplicity/set-vs-multiset conventions, and exact cardinalities may not be relaxed silently.
Any asymptotic/eventual claim retains the same limiting variable and full-sequence requirement.
The frozen current Lean signature remains semantically consistent with the prose contract; binder types and predicates may not be altered merely to make the theorem easier to prove.
The extremal direction and the distinction between minimal/maximal and minimum/maximum.
known_traps: QUANTIFIER SLIP: exchanging ∀ and ∃, moving an epsilon/constant after the limiting variable, or replacing “all sufficiently large” by “infinitely many”.
SAMPLED-TO-UNIVERSAL: checking many finite instances and promoting the observation to an unrestricted theorem without a valid finite-reduction theorem.
DOMAIN DRIFT: proving a translated/scaled/relaxed version without an exact map back to the original domain, endpoints, and discrete constraints.
STRENGTH CONFUSION: refuting a stronger folklore conjecture does not refute the canonical claim; proving a weaker statement does not prove it.

FORMAL/PROSE DRIFT: a Lean proof is acceptable only if the exact frozen signature is semantically the same target. `answer(sorry)` or independently filled answer metavariables are not permission to choose an easier proposition/function.
BOUND-AS-ANSWER TRAP: an improved record bound or candidate constant is not a determination unless matching lower/upper (or necessary/sufficient) proofs establish exactness.
ASYMPTOTIC CONSTANT DRIFT: hidden constants cannot depend on the main variable, and one-sided O/Ω bounds do not establish Θ/asymptotic equivalence.
non_results: A theorem for only a selected finite set of parameter values when the statement is uniform or asymptotic.
A result only on a favorable subsequence, density-one subset, almost-everywhere set, or “generic” family when the canonical statement requires the full sequence/all objects.
A numerical fit, heuristic, Monte Carlo result, floating-point experiment, or finite computation without a proved finite-reduction/transfer theorem to the canonical claim.
A restricted-family result obtained by adding hypotheses not present in the statement, unless those hypotheses are proved without loss of generality for every canonical instance.
A conditional theorem whose decisive premise is an unproved conjecture of comparable strength.
A reduction to an equivalent-strength open problem, a tautological rephrasing, or a definition of the requested answer in terms of the original unresolved predicate.
A continuous/real-valued/LP/SDP relaxation without a proved integrality or exact-transfer theorem when the canonical objects are discrete.
A stronger-looking statement in a different normalization/domain that does not formally imply the canonical statement.
Any isolated improved upper or lower bound that does not determine the requested value/order/classification.
A conjectured optimal constant/exponent/class based on computation without matching achievability and impossibility proofs.
Declaring the residual cases “open” instead of resolving them or proving genuine independence.
A one-sided asymptotic estimate when the target asks for an equality, equivalence, limit, or two-sided order.
A bound with a constant depending on the limiting variable or on hidden arithmetic data of that variable.
Replacing liminf by limsup, a full limit by a limsup/liminf statement, or divergence by unboundedness on a sparse subsequence.
A feasible construction or a bound on the extremal value without the complementary proof showing optimality/exact extremality.
permitted_background: Definitions and elementary facts in the named mathematical domain, with every imported theorem used only under its exact published/formal hypotheses.

Standard algebraic, combinatorial, analytic, probabilistic, number-theoretic, set-theoretic, and asymptotic lemmas needed to manipulate the objects appearing in the statement; no theorem equivalent in strength to the target may be assumed.

Exact finite computation, SAT/SMT/MILP, interval arithmetic, symbolic algebra, exhaustive enumeration, or custom verified tooling may be used as a lemma/certificate when its finite search space and transfer to the unrestricted claim are proved.
Lean/Mathlib or another proof assistant may certify intermediate and final results; kernel acceptance does not by itself excuse a semantic mismatch with the canonical statement.
